zh.title: ASELSAN在科尼亞測試TB2電子戰系統
zh.summary: ASELSAN在土耳其科尼亞測試TB2電子戰莢艙；18國代表觀摩
body: ASELSAN於9月18日宣布，在土耳其科尼亞舉行示範，將三款機載電子戰與雷達莢艙搭載於Bayraktar TB2無人機上試飛，共有18國防務代表團觀摩。
試驗系統包括ANTIDOT 2ES 100電子支援莢艙、ANTIDOT 2EA 200電子攻擊莢艙與FULMAR 200合成孔徑雷達莢艙。兩個ANTIDOT莢艙由一架TB2攜帶，FULMAR 200由另一架TB2攜帶，兩機共同執行同一情境。
第一階段中，電子支援莢艙偵測目標雷達並確定位置，ANTIDOT 2EA 200隨後利用該定位資料實施電子攻擊，ASELSAN表示此使攜帶莢艙的TB2得以在不被偵測下接近目標。
第二階段則由電子支援莢艙定位另一發射源，將位置傳予FULMAR 200，後者產出目標區域的高解析度SAR影像。
ASELSAN指出，這是ANTIDOT首次在TB2上對真實雷達系統測試，也是兩大莢艙家族首度聯合示範。公司未透露作為目標的雷達系統型號。
此配置針對壓制敵防空（SEAD）任務，過往需專用有人機型。ASELSAN 6月曾在較大型的Bayraktar TB3外掛相同ANTIDOT組合，7月並帶赴范堡羅航展。移植至TB2或提供較低成本路徑，TB2為Baykar出口最廣機型，據報已有36國簽署協議，現有用戶原則上可增裝莢艙式電子戰能力而無需購新機身。

en.title: ASELSAN demonstrates electronic warfare pods on Bayraktar TB2 drones in Konya trial
en.summary: ASELSAN tests electronic warfare pods on Bayraktar TB2 drones in Konya; 18 nations observe
body: ASELSAN announced on September 18 that it had flown three airborne electronic warfare and radar pods on Bayraktar TB2 drones during a demonstration in Konya, Turkey, attended by defense delegations from 18 countries.

The systems involved were the ANTIDOT 2ES 100 electronic support pod, the ANTIDOT 2EA 200 electronic attack pod, and the FULMAR 200 synthetic aperture radar pod. According to ASELSAN, the two ANTIDOT pods were carried by one TB2 and the FULMAR 200 by a second aircraft, with both drones working the same scenario.

In the first sequence described by the company, the electronic support pod detected a target radar in flight and established its position. The ANTIDOT 2EA 200 then conducted an electronic attack on that radar using the targeting data the support pod had generated. ASELSAN said the result allowed the TB2 carrying the pods to approach the target without being detected.
In the second sequence, the electronic support pod located a different emitter and passed its position to the FULMAR 200, which produced a high-resolution SAR image of the target area.

ASELSAN said the activity marked the first time ANTIDOT had been tested against real radar systems while carried on a TB2, and the first demonstration of the two pod families working together. The company did not identify the radar systems used as targets.

The configuration is aimed at the suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), a mission set that has historically required dedicated crewed aircraft. ASELSAN showed the same ANTIDOT pair mounted externally on the larger Bayraktar TB3 in June 2026, a configuration it described at the time as a world first, and brought both pods and the FULMAR radars to Farnborough in July 2026. Moving the pair onto the TB2 could provide a lower-cost route to that capability, although ASELSAN has not disclosed the cost of the pods or their integration. The TB2 is the most widely exported drone in Baykar's range, with the company reporting agreements covering the type in 36 countries. Existing operators could, in principle, add a pod-based electronic warfare capability without buying a new airframe.

zh.title: BAE系統公司公布小型機載電子戰酬載 2027年投產
zh.summary: BAE Systems公布Shadow EW系列酬載；第一款2027年投產
body: BAE Systems公司公布一系列名為Shadow EW的電子戰酬載，重量約3公斤（7磅），設計用於小型飛機與無人機，提供電子感測、目標鎖定與欺敵能力。
該公司表示，第一款型號Shadow EW 100預定於2027年投產，重量為3.3公斤（7.2磅），涵蓋頻率範圍為70 MHz至6 GHz，功耗低於150瓦。
第二款Shadow EW 120規劃於2028年推出，頻率範圍向下延伸至5 MHz；第三款Shadow EW 500預計在2029年推出，重量約3.2公斤（7磅），涵蓋10 MHz至18 GHz，並新增無線電頻率測向與地理定位功能，功耗可達250瓦。
BAE Systems尚未公布客戶、整合合約或搭載平台。不過，報導指出其製造將在愛荷華州錫達拉皮茲進行。

en.title: BAE Systems unveils Shadow EW payloads for small aircraft, production from 2027
en.summary: BAE Systems unveils Shadow EW payloads for small aircraft; Shadow EW 100 production 2027
body: BAE Systems has unveiled a family of electronic warfare payloads weighing around 3 kilograms (7 pounds), designed to bring electronic sensing, targeting, and deception capabilities to small aircraft and drones.
The first variant, Shadow EW 100, is scheduled for production in 2027, weighing 3.3 kilograms (7.2 pounds) and covering frequencies from 70 MHz to 6 GHz while consuming less than 150 watts.

Shadow EW 120, planned for 2028, extends coverage down to 5 MHz. The third variant, Shadow EW 500, expected in 2029, weighs approximately 3.2 kilograms (7 pounds), covers 10 MHz to 18 GHz, adds radio-frequency direction finding and geolocation, and reaches 250 watts of power consumption.
BAE Systems has yet to announce a customer, integration contract, or platform. The company plans manufacturing in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, with software and design work in Nashua, New Hampshire.
